newsitem.title: USA: Lexington Cty, S.C., advances convention center.
newsitem.headline: Lexington Cty, S.C., advances convention center.

text.p: South Carolina's Lexington County Council gave preliminary approval to a hotel tax increase to finance a downtown convention and sports center, The State newspaper reported Tuesday.
The council approved the proposal 8-0 Monday night in the second of three needed votes. The final vote will follow a public hearing in December.

The proposal would increase the county's hotel bed tax to five percent from two percent. It would raise $700,000 a year for the $15 million meeting center, which would be paired with a new $48 million basketball arena for the University of South Carolina.
The state has tentatively allocated some money for the basketball arena, but the money could go elsewhere unless a solid financial plan is approved.

The plan calls for a revenue sharing agreement among the City of Columbia and Lexington and Richland counties. It would give the counties some of the revenues from hotels built near the convention center. The city has already raised its hotel tax as part of the plan.
